source.title: Linear Transformers with Learnable Kernel Functions are Better In-Context Models
source.authors: Yaroslav Aksenov; Nikita Balagansky; S. Vaina; B. Shaposhnikov; Alexey Gorbatovski; Daniil Gavrilov

page_placements.theme: Induction-style recall and copying in non-attention and hybrid architectures

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates associative recall and in-context learning in linear-transformer architectures, but does not test the formation, function, prevalence, or training dynamics of induction heads as described in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites work on induction heads and measures MQAR retrieval, associative-token perplexity, and attention-map overlap. These are related to the claim's subject but do not identify or test induction heads, their formation during training, or their role in large-transformer in-context learning. The study also reports few-shot benchmark results, but does not test the mechanisms behind that performance.
record.test_reason: The paper benchmarks a new linear-attention kernel (ReBased) on MQAR, Pile associative-token perplexity and few-shot tasks. It uses the induction-head copying idea from Olsson et al. as a tool: it motivates AR perplexity, and the Section 5.6 IoU analysis assumes second-layer copying. It does not identify induction heads, track their formation, or test any version. In the Section 5.6 model, the previous-token step is a fixed convolution rather than a learned previous-token head, so V1 composition is built in, not observed. The IoU and accuracy results compare the authors' architecture with baselines, which is T4 rather than T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude that ReBased's attention maps resemble softmax attention more than Based's do. They add that attention still clearly beats sub-quadratic models on MQAR as sequence length grows. They state that results are limited to academic-scale models.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and compares linear-transformer and other architectures on MQAR and language modeling; it does not reproduce the original induction-head measurements or training analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with sequence length, model dimension, and kernel modification; the reported long-sequence MQAR results differ from the short-sequence results.

fits_no_version.finding: ReBased has higher mean MQAR accuracy than Based at sequence lengths 256 (0.63 vs 0.58) and 2048 (0.61 vs 0.51). Attention's retrieval-position IoU is far higher (0.999 vs 0.157/0.173), even though MQAR accuracy is similar (1 vs 0.956/0.957).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear-attention hybrids can reach near-attention MQAR accuracy while their attention maps align far less with the copy targets than softmax attention.

fits_no_version.finding: On Pile, AR-token perplexity is Attention 3.07, Based 3.27 and ReBased 3.25.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested ~150M Pile models, linear-attention variants remain worse than softmax attention on associative-recall tokens.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2024
record.problems: The authors state that experiments are limited to academic-scale models. MQAR accuracy and associative-token perplexity are indirect measures for induction-head claims; the attention-map analysis measures retrieval-position overlap, not head formation or causal contribution. Uncertainty is reported for the ablation accuracies but not for the Pile perplexities or IoU results.
record.rows_left_out: Few-shot benchmark results in Tables 3 and 4 were left out because they report task scores without measuring copying, induction-head behaviour, or the mechanism carrying few-shot learning. Other MQAR figure-only comparisons were not separately extracted; the text gives aggregate qualitative comparisons in Section 5.2 but no exact values.

untested.parts: No learned previous-token head and no composition analysis. In Section 5.6 the first layer is a fixed previous-token convolution, and the models are not attention-only.
No training trajectory, phase change or loss bump is measured.
No link is tested between induction heads and loss falling with token index in large models.
Linear-attention models solve MQAR with diffuse attention (IoU 0.157/0.173), but induction heads are not identified across families or runs.
Data and training setup are not varied with respect to induction-head formation.
Few-shot scores (Tables 3–4) are reported without mechanism attribution.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from discusses/T6 to uses_without_test/T4. The paper uses the induction-head copying mechanism (Olsson et al.) as the rationale for its AR-perplexity and IoU measures, but reports only comparisons of its own architecture. All row links to 'none' are kept. T19 has an empty numbers_found field, but its value of 1 matches Table 5.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not identify induction heads or test their composition with a previous-token head, nor does it test the specified [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism in small attention-only transformers.
No induction-head formation trajectory, training-loss bump, or timing comparison with an in-context-learning gain is measured.
The study does not test whether induction heads explain most in-context learning in large transformers, or measure loss by token index in those models.
The study does not survey induction behaviour across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
The study does not vary data or training setup to test whether induction heads form or whether in-context learning persists.
Few-shot benchmark performance is reported, but the study does not test which heads or mechanisms carry few-shot learning.
The study does not measure induction-head formation over training or test whether it comprises multiple transitions.

relation.reason: Section 5.6 uses the earlier previous-token and second-layer copying mechanism to construct its analysis, fixing the first-layer convolution to attend to the previous token.

tranche.reason: The study uses associative copying to motivate architecture benchmarks and retrieval-position analysis. It reports method performance without testing spontaneous induction-head formation, learned previous-token composition, or the other claim versions.

source_check.notes: Table 1 uses 32 retrieval pairs at both sequence lengths. Table 5 uses sequence length 128, 32 retrieval pairs, and a fixed previous-token first layer; its alignment scores do not establish spontaneous mechanism formation. The recorded authors' conclusion matches Sections 6–7.
